items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: trial by fire with Philly Joe Jones and Milt Hinton and Tony, and the girl singer was Carmen McRae.

ctx.x: Okay. So I didn’t pay much attention, I liked it all right, and then my mother would make me take piano lessons at the Peabody Conservatory which I was not a good student. I really cheated ‘cause I didn’t really want to learn to read so I used to watch this fat lady

play, I would watch her hands and imitate her. So it didn’t really take, but let’s see, the first one to turn me on was Fats Waller. My brother had these Fats Waller records. And the way he played the piano, still, if you listen, it had an equilibrium and a balance, it’s very rare even now. And there were certain little figures. I didn’t really — I tried a little bit to play like him, but like a lot of kids I would just imitate little licks here and there. And early on I realized well I’m not really ever going to…
But were you reading like chord symbols at the time? Could you do that?
